spec: Build a REST API for personal notes. Users can create, list, fetch, update and delete notes. Each note has a title, body and timestamps. Notes are stored in DynamoDB.

plan.summary: A REST API for managing personal notes with full CRUD operations. Users can create, list, fetch, update, and delete notes, each containing a title, body, and creation/update timestamps. Notes are persisted in DynamoDB.

endpoints.purpose: Create a new note with title and body; sets timestamps.
Fetch a single note by its ID.
Update an existing note's title and/or body; updates the updated_at timestamp.
Delete a note by its ID.

aws_resources.name: notes_table
aws_resources.justification: Primary persistent storage for note items, explicitly required by the spec for storing notes.

aws_resources.name: notes_api_role
aws_resources.justification: Execution role granting the application permission to read/write the DynamoDB notes table.

aws_resources.name: notes_api_logs
aws_resources.justification: Captures application and request logs for observability and debugging of the API.

assumptions: No authentication or multi-user isolation was specified; the API is treated as single-tenant with no auth layer.
note_id is generated server-side as a UUID string and used as the DynamoDB partition key.
Timestamps (created_at, updated_at) are stored as ISO8601 strings set by the server.
The API returns and accepts JSON, so FastAPI was chosen.
'List notes' performs a full table scan since no filtering or pagination was specified.
The API runs as a containerized/ASGI service rather than as a Lambda, so no API Gateway or Lambda resources were provisioned.
